data.description: Admission can be rescheduled if the plasma glucose level is not within range on Day 1
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop Criterion)
data.description: Insulin infusion is stopped once the target hypoglycemia threshold is reached
data.text: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale 'During Induction' Trigger
data.description: Timepoint defined by plasma glucose threshold during hypoglycemia induction
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Condition (First 6 Patients)
data.description: Safety data review required before remaining patients are dosed
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2, and the remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of the safety. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, from these patients after they complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Fasting Condition for Treatment Period Laboratory Samples
data.description: Fasting requirement at Periods 1 and 2; not required at screening or follow-up
data.text: At Periods 1 and 2, samples should be collected from patients who have fasted at least 8 hours before any study procedures. Patients do not need to fast for samples at screening or follow-up.

data.name: TE ADA Positivity Requiring Additional Follow-up
data.description: Patients positive for treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies at follow-up require additional immunogenicity follow-up
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up. Samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Drug Hypersensitivity Reaction Sampling Condition
data.description: Additional immunogenicity sampling triggered by hypersensitivity reaction
data.text: In the event of drug hypersensitivity reactions (immediate or non-immediate), samples will be collected as close to event onset as possible, at event resolution, and 30 days following the event.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability Condition
data.description: Review of insulin regimen before hypoglycemia induction procedure
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Plasma Glucose Stability Before Discharge
data.description: Investigator must confirm plasma glucose stability after carbohydrate-rich meal
data.text: After completion of all PK sampling, patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal. The investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable. A prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed.

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Primary analysis success criterion
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the NIM of 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Condition
data.description: Replacement of discontinued patients to reach required completers
data.text: If patients discontinue from the study before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled, if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: Inadvertently Enrolled Patient Continuation Condition
data.description: Conditions under which an inadvertently enrolled patient may continue
data.text: If the sponsor or investigator identifies a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled, a discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue in the study. If both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition (Randomization)
data.text: Patients will undergo a screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment. Prior to the study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients will be randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or vice versa).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition
data.text: Patients may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration; a washout period of 3 to 14 days follows Period 1 dosing.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 Transition
data.text: Patients will be administered a single dose in Periods 1 and 2, which will be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days. Procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment (within 28±2 days after last study treatment).

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up with immunogenicity samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Treatment Sequence Crossover (Arm Transition)
data.text: Randomized crossover: patients receive either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or IMG in Period 1 and LY900018 in Period 2.

data.name: Dosing Trigger Based on Bedside Plasma Glucose
data.text: Once bedside PG reaches <60 mg/dL, the insulin infusion is stopped and approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4); a prandial insulin dose and carbohydrate-rich meal will be administered as needed with investigator confirming PG stability.

data.name: Rescheduling of Admission/Dosing
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Discontinuation from the Study - Other Research Participation
data.text: Enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or enrollment in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation from the Study - Medical/Safety/Regulatory
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation from the Study - Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation from the Study - Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria was inadvertently enrolled, the patient must be discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree it is medically appropriate to continue, with documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP, with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Study-Level Safety Stopping Rule
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED)
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities; the Follow-up/ED visit serves as the early discontinuation visit.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome and attendance at the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment; additional TE ADA follow-up completed if applicable.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent attempts by site personnel.

data.name: Study Discontinuation by Sponsor/Investigator
data.description: The entire study may be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor following review of safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1.

data.name: Completion of TE ADA Follow-up
data.description: TE ADA follow-up ends when the antibody titer returns to baseline (within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision Before Dosing Remaining Patients
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1 (having received LY900018 in Period 2), the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review safety data; remaining patients are dosed only after safety confirmation, otherwise the study may be stopped.

data.name: Dosing Day Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose Check)
data.description: At admission/Day 1, if plasma glucose is not 90 to 250 mg/dL, admission is rescheduled; insulin regimen reviewed for acceptability to undergo hypoglycemia induction.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Endpoint and Study Drug Administration Decision
data.description: Insulin infusion stopped when bedside PG <60 mg/dL; study treatment administered approximately 5 minutes later, defining Time = 0 min.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration once PG is stable after a carbohydrate-rich meal; patient may remain inpatient at the discretion of the investigator.

data.name: TE ADA Follow-up Decision
data.description: At Follow-up/ED, if treatment-emergent ADA are detected, the patient enters additional immunogenicity follow-up every 12 weeks (84±7 days).

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis of treatment success percentages; non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference (IMG - LY900018) is less than 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Decision
data.description: Discontinued patients may be replaced, not exceeding 75 enrolled, to ensure at least 66 completers (≥30 T1DM and ≥30 T2DM).
